list: The official 55 trophies, frozen 2026-11-18: 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze.
note: Names, descriptions and grades are exactly as PlayStation publishes them (via Exophase and PSNProfiles, which agree on every entry). Every guide below is written in our own words from those official descriptions and the PSN progress targets; where the game has only just launched and a spot is not pinned down yet, the guide says so plainly instead of inventing a location.

sources.exophase: Exophase — official trophy list (names, descriptions, grades): https://www.exophase.com/game/grand-theft-auto-vi-psn/trophies/
sources.own: Our own advice, built from the official description — not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum pops on its own the moment the other 54 trophies are yours — there is no extra task behind it. Work the roadmap in this guide in order (story, then side strands and activities, then collectibles, then the grinds) and it lands last, as it should. Nothing here can be missed outright: every trophy can be earned in free roam or by replaying a mission.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: The very first story mission, Gone Fishing, opens the game. Follow the on-screen prompts, play through the opening beats, and the trophy pops when the mission ends. It cannot be missed — it is the front door to the story, and every player walks through it.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Play through every mission in Chapter 1 until the chapter closes. Story trophies pop as the plot moves, so there is nothing special to do — just keep following the story markers. If you are mopping up later, chapter progress is tracked in the pause menu.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 2 the same way: play its missions in order until the chapter ends. The name is printed exactly as PlayStation publishes it, asterisks included. No side content is needed for this one — the story alone carries it.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Chapter 3's missions take you deeper into Vice City itself. Clear them in story order and the trophy pops at the chapter close. This is a good point to start ticking off side activities between missions — the map is wide open by now and several activity trophies are cheapest to start early.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: The last full chapter before the finale. Finish its missions and this trophy pops, leaving only the final mission for the gold. Before you push on, check the missables page — a few one-moment trophies below are easiest to grab while the story is still moving.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: The gold for finishing the story: complete the final mission and the credits roll with this trophy. It is the natural end of roadmap stage 1. If you have been saving side content for after the story, the whole map stays open once the finale is done, so nothing is locked away by finishing.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is one named story mission, and this trophy is tied to finishing it. Missable only in the narrow sense that it belongs to a single story moment — if you somehow pass it without the pop, replay the mission from the pause menu's replay list and it will trigger on completion. Play it normally the first time; no special approach is needed.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is a set-piece story mission, and the trophy is its completion reward. As with the other mission trophies, the 'missable' flag means it lives in one story moment — mission replay covers you if anything goes wrong on the first run. Bring your best driving and shooting to the heist itself; the trophy only asks that you finish it.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Child's Play is a single story mission — finish it and the trophy pops. Flagged missable because it is bound to that one mission, not because it is hard: replay the mission from the pause menu if you need a second run. Nothing in the mission needs a special route or optional objective for the trophy itself.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Headliners is the mission behind this trophy — complete it and DWNFALL is yours. It is flagged because it belongs to one story beat; mission replay is the safety net if the first attempt glitches. Play the mission through to its end card and do not quit out early.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: VCIA Takedown is the airport mission, and finishing it earns Hi-Jacked. One story moment, so flagged missable — replay it from the pause menu if the pop does not land first time. The airport setting also matters for a later trophy (Catch Me If You Can), so keep the VCIA layout in mind while you are there.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory is the mission for this trophy — complete it to earn Snow Storm. Like the other mission trophies it is flagged only because it is tied to one story moment; a replay from the pause menu fixes a missed pop. Finish the operation and move on — the trophy asks for nothing extra.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: The gold for 100% completion — the last big trophy for most players, and the one this whole guide is built around. The in-game stats page tracks your percentage: story, stranger strands, activities, collectibles and the grinds all feed it. Work the roadmap in order and watch the percentage climb; the final few percent are almost always a collectible set or a challenge count, so use the filters on this page to find what is left.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: PSN tracks this one to 250 stunts — jumps, near-misses, drifts and airtime all count toward the total, and it builds up naturally if you drive hard. To grind it deliberately, chain stunt jumps and long airtime off ramps and hills; every clean stunt adds one. Save this grind for stage 4, after the story, when you can focus on driving without mission pressure.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: There are 9 activity types across Leonida — races, fishing, shooting range, drone races, arcade games, bowling, meditation, hunting and more. Try each one once and the trophy pops. Do this early in stage 2: it is a sampler that shows you which activities you enjoy before you commit to their longer trophies, and it costs almost nothing.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: PSN tracks 42 Shooting Range challenges, and this silver wants a gold medal in every one of them. Visit the range between missions to learn the drills, then grind the golds in stage 4 when your aim and weapon handling are at their best. Slow down for accuracy over speed on the precision drills — gold is about clean hits, not fast ones.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: There are 14 Top Fun drone race locations across the map, and you need a win at each one. Learn one course at a time — drones handle nothing like cars, so brake early for the gates and cut corners only when you can see the next gate. Tick them off as you explore in stage 3; the map markers make it easy to plan a route through several at once.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — different courses, not the same one 20 times. Mix cars, bikes and boats as the race types allow, and pick a vehicle class you are comfortable with rather than the fastest on paper. Races unlock as you explore, so work through the map's race markers in stage 3 and the count climbs steadily.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Find Cal and take him on in a fishing challenge — then out-fish him. Watch the line tension and reel in steady bursts rather than holding the trigger down; the fish fights in runs, and you win by letting it tire itself out between pulls. One win is all it takes, and fishing spots are also good quiet places to relax between missions.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Walk into any arcade, pick a cabinet and finish one full game — any game, any score. This is the easiest trophy on the list and a good first tick in stage 2. Arcade games are also a cheap way to sample the activity types for Master of None, so do this one while you are there.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Andy has a strand of side missions, and this trophy is for finishing the last of them. Look for Andy's marker on the map, work through his jobs in order, and the trophy pops at the end of his final mission. Side strands like this are the heart of stage 2 — do them before the collectible grind, while the map still feels fresh.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Kenton's strand ends with this trophy: finish his final mission. Kenton's jobs lean toward the water, so keep a fast boat handy and expect the finale to use it. If his marker is not showing yet, push the story forward — stranger strands open up as the chapters progress.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Billy's final mission closes his strand and earns The Lone Rider. His jobs are solo affairs — the name is the hint — so expect to ride out alone rather than with your partner. Clear his earlier missions first; the strand only offers its finale once the rest are done.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: The silver for finishing 8 full stranger strands — the Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone finales on this list count toward it, plus three more strangers you will meet around Leonida. Watch for the '?' markers on the map and take every strand you find; each one is a short story of its own. This is the stage 2 centerpiece, so do not rush past the strangers while chasing the main plot.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Randy's strand is about moving product, and its final mission earns Supply & Demand. Work through his jobs in order — they get bigger as the strand goes on — and keep some cash in reserve for the finale's setup. Like the other stranger finales, it counts toward the Strangers & Freaks silver.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Tyrone's final mission closes his strand and pops Spin On This! His jobs have a music-scene flavor, so expect the finale to be loud and public. Finish his earlier missions first — the strand gates its finale behind them — and it counts toward Strangers & Freaks as well.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: There are 18 meditation spots scattered across Leonida, usually in quiet, scenic places — clifftops, beaches, parks. Sit and meditate at each one; PSN tracks the count to 18. Fold this into your stage 3 exploration route: when you are passing a region for another collectible, check the meditation spots there too and save yourself a second trip.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Bret wants one specific animal hunted — a unique beast, not just any wildlife. Track it with the hunting tools, move quietly, and take the shot when it is clean; a rushed shot spooks it and wastes the stalk. The exact animal and its territory are not pinned down in the official description, so follow Bret's directions in-game and check the hunting markers before you set out.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Collectible cards are hidden around Leonida in sets, and this silver needs 3 full sets completed. Cards turn up in shops, houses, hideouts and odd corners — search thoroughly and trade duplicates if the game allows it. This is a stage 3 grind: do it alongside the WAiNK and vehicle hunts, since all three reward the same habit of poking into every corner of the map.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: WAiNK It is the in-game photo/sharing gag, and PSN tracks it to 100 locations — snap it at landmarks, viewpoints and odd spots all over Leonida. The count only moves at new locations, so keep moving: pair this with the exploration trophy and tick WAiNK spots off region by region. It is a long, pleasant grind rather than a hard one.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Challenges are the game's small side objectives — feats, dares and one-off tasks — and PSN tracks them to 50. They pile up naturally while you chase the other trophies, so check the challenge list in the pause menu during stage 4 and knock out the easy ones first. The last few are usually the fiddly ones; leave them until the rest of the list is nearly done.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Get to a 4-star wanted level while your partner is with you, then lose the heat together and escape. The trick is the escape, not the wanted level: break line of sight, get off the main roads, and use alleys, tunnels or water to shake the search. Do it with your partner nearby — the trophy only counts when you are together when the heat drops.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob three shops in a row with your partner, keeping your wanted level the whole time — the streak breaks if the heat drops between robberies. Pick three shops close together, move fast between them, and keep the getaway car pointed at the next target before you walk in. If the heat drops, the count resets, so plan the route first and hit all three in one run.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: PSN tracks vehicle discovery to 100 — just getting into a new vehicle counts it as discovered. Walk through car parks, dealerships and docks and hop into everything you have not driven yet; rare spawns hide in specific neighborhoods, so vary your routes. Pair this with the Scooter Bros registrations and the garage purchases — the same vehicle-hunting habit feeds all three.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Combat Focus slows time and sharpens your aim — trigger it with at least five enemies in view and drop all five before it ends. The easiest setup is a gang shootout or a wanted-level standoff where enemies bunch up: wait until they are clustered, then activate and work left to right. If you only get four, the count resets, so set the scene before you spend the meter.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: At Vice City International Airport, leave in a way the airport did not schedule — steal a plane and take off without clearance, or otherwise depart on your own terms. Flagged missable because it is tied to one specific place and one bold move: get to the runways, grab an aircraft, and get airborne before security closes in. If it does not pop, try a different aircraft or runway — the trigger is the unscheduled departure itself.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The Rhino is the army tank, and this trophy is about getting up close with one — or several. The description is deliberately cryptic, so treat it as a dare: find a Rhino (high wanted levels and military areas are where they appear), survive the encounter, and see what the game counts. Come with heavy weapons and a fast escape vehicle; tanks do not forgive slow getaways.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store and stay completely undetected while you do it — no alarms, no spotted cameras, no witnesses raising the alarm. Plan the approach: scout the store first, go in quiet, and leave before anyone notices. Flagged missable because a detected attempt fails the condition, but you can retry the robbery until you get a clean run, so treat a failed attempt as a rehearsal.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob five bank vaults and escape after each one — PSN tracks the count to 5. Bank jobs need planning: scout the bank, pick your entry and exit, and have the getaway ready before you go in loud. Do them spread across stage 3 rather than back-to-back; the heat after each one is serious, and a cool-down between jobs keeps the streak alive.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Armored trucks roam the highways — stop one, crack it open, take the cash and escape. Ram it off the road or block it, deal with the guards, grab the loot and vanish before the response arrives. One clean robbery and escape is all it takes, and trucks respawn, so a failed first try costs you nothing but time.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Leonida has 52 named areas and this trophy wants all of them visited. Drive, fly and sail the map methodically — the in-game map shades in as you go, so the blank patches show you where you still need to be. Fold this into every other stage 3 hunt: meditation spots, WAiNK locations and card sets all live in the same corners you need to visit anyway.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: There are 9 gangs running illegal operations across Leonida, and this trophy wants one operation robbed from each of them. Learn which gang holds which turf — operations show up as you explore and as the story introduces each crew — then hit one per gang. Expect each gang to defend its turf differently, so scout before you strike.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: The easiest trophy with the best view: go to Ocean Beach, order a cocktail at a beachfront spot, and enjoy it. No skill needed, no grind — just show up and sit down. Do it early in stage 2 as a palate cleanser between harder trophies; the ellipsis in the name is a nod to where it all began.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Drive into a vehicle showroom and smash your way out through the glass, in classic GTA style — the trophy is for the exit, not the entrance. Flagged missable because it is one specific stunt in one specific place: pick a showroom with a big glass front, build speed inside, and go straight through. If the pop does not land, try another showroom — the trigger is the smash-out itself.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Head to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley and bowl a proper game — follow through on your throws, as the description hints. One full game is enough; you do not need a high score, just a completed game at that specific alley. It is a gentle stage 2 trophy and a nice nod to the series' past — bring your partner along for the full effect.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: The description is deliberately vague — a partnership moment with mass appeal — and the exact trigger is not pinned down in the official list. The honest read: it is tied to doing something notable together with your partner that draws a crowd or goes public. Keep playing the partner missions and shared activities in stage 2 and watch for a moment that feels like a show; this guide will be updated once the community pins the trigger down.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: PSN tracks this one to 500 — choices made across the game, for better or worse. Every dialogue choice, moral call and side decision feeds the count, so it grows on its own through a full playthrough. If you are short in stage 4, revisit choice-heavy missions and side content; the count is about volume, not picking the 'right' answers.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Fail something, then succeed on the second try — that is the whole trophy. Flagged missable because it needs a specific sequence: a failed attempt followed immediately by a success. The cleanest way is to deliberately fail something low-stakes (a race, a challenge, a minigame), then win it on the very next attempt. Do not let a third attempt intervene — second time really is the charm here.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Something strange is out there in Leonida, and this trophy is for finding it — the kind of odd, unexplained encounter the series hides in its corners. The official description gives no location, so the honest advice is to explore the weird places: remote swamps, deserted stretches, anywhere that feels wrong at night. When you see something you cannot explain, you have probably found it.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: A melee drive-by means leaning out of a moving vehicle and swinging a melee weapon at someone as you pass — bowl them over with it. Flagged missable because it is a specific move that is easy to do wrong: slow the car to a crawl beside a pedestrian, lean out, and time the swing as you roll past. Practice on a quiet street before you try it in traffic.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Marked Bills are dirty money from heists and robberies, and your contacts will launder them for a cut — PSN tracks the laundered total to $250,000. Bank jobs, armored trucks and gang operations all produce marked bills, so this trophy fills itself if you keep robbing through stage 3. In stage 4, check your contacts and launder whatever is left; the trophy counts what you earn through the wash, not what you hold.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops — clothes, weapons, food, anything with a price tag counts toward the total. You will cover a good chunk of it just by gearing up through the story, so do not force it early. In stage 4, check the total in your stats and top it up with a shopping spree: weapons and high-end clothes are the fastest way to close the gap.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: There are 8 garage properties to buy across Leonida, and this trophy wants all of them in your name. Garages are bought through the in-game property listings — save your cash for them in stage 3 rather than spending it all on cars, and buy each one as you find it. Owning them also gives you somewhere to keep the 100 vehicles you are discovering for Whip It Good.
sources: Our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: The Scooter Bros app lets you register vehicles, and this trophy wants 10 of them on the books. Any vehicle you drive can be registered, so as you discover the 100 for Whip It Good, register the keepers along the way — ten registrations is a small slice of the discovery total. Open the app, pick a vehicle you own or have found, and register it; repeat until the count hits 10.
sources: Our own advice from the official description
